info.title: KoLo Gateway API
info.description: HTTP surface of one Kurahi gateway (one per identity). Generated from the route registry in src/gateway/http-routes.ts; the gateway serves the live copy at GET /doc. Every operation names its token class in `x-kolo-scope`. All HTTP requests share a per-IP sliding window (x-kolo-rate-limit) and credential-bearing requests also count against a 20/min credential-attempt limiter; both answer 429 with Retry-After. Routes that exist but are not described operation by operation are listed in x-kolo-undocumented-routes with the reason.

post.summary: Run a Code Mode script
post.description: Runs one agent-written JavaScript/TypeScript script in a sandboxed worker thread. The script calls the session's tools as `await tools.<name>({...})` and returns a value: one round trip instead of one call per tool. Tools are the session agent's policy-filtered list (core, plugin, `mcp:<server>:<tool>`); `allowTools` narrows it further. Limits: wall clock (default 60 s), heap, tool calls per script (default 200). Every tool call is audited under the run id. A backend with tools=none answers 403.

x-kolo-rate-limit.credentialAttempts: only when the request carries credentials and fails with 401/403

gatewayToken.description: Gateway shared secret (token or password mode) as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`. The secret lives in the gateway's 0600 token file, never in config or argv.

adminSession.name: kolo_session
adminSession.description: Invite-flow session with the admin role: the `kolo_session` cookie set by POST /api/auth/redeem (a Bearer session token is accepted too).

ssoSession.description: SSO session token (`kss_…`) of a person who signed in through the organisation's identity provider (OIDC or SAML), as `Authorization: Bearer`. The person's roles give the scope; auditors may also read the audit chain and evidence.

scimToken.description: Provisioning token from `gateway.identity.scim.token` (secrets store), presented by the identity provider's SCIM client.

pairToken.description: Pairing access token (`kpa_…`) from POST /api/pair/redeem or /api/pair/refresh, as `Authorization: Bearer`. Bound to the device key that redeemed the invitation and carrying one scope (observe < attach < admin); `x-kolo-min-scope` on the operation is the least scope it accepts. Short-lived; rotate with the refresh token.

hookToken.name: X-KoLo-Token
hookToken.description: hooks.token from config, as `X-KoLo-Token` or `Authorization: Bearer`. A `?token=` query parameter still works but is deprecated (URLs leak into logs).

migrateKey.name: X-Migrate-Key
migrateKey.description: INVITE_SIGNING_KEY from the gateway environment (timing-safe compare).

pluginSignature.name: X-Provider-Signature
pluginSignature.description: Channel webhooks are verified by the owning plugin with the provider's own scheme (for example X-Line-Signature HMAC, Slack signing secret). The header name varies.

Paths are per Slack account config and registered when the channel starts; verified with the Slack signing secret by the channel. Registered paths appear in the live GET /doc.
Keeps the pre-registry answers for paths no route declares: 405 for non-GET, JSON 404 for unknown GET subpaths (after the admin auth gate).

x-kolo-undocumented-routes.reason: Registered by plugins at runtime; each verifies its provider's signature. Routes registered with registerPluginHttpRoute/registerHttpRoute are listed as operations in the live GET /doc (auth: plugin); catch-all registerHttpHandler handlers cannot be described.
Static assets. Non-local clients need the gateway token (M2a remote gate); local direct clients are exempt.

x-kolo-undocumented-routes.summary: Canvas host files and live-reload WebSocket
x-kolo-undocumented-routes.reason: Serves the agent canvas directory as static files plus a live-reload upgrade; gated for non-local clients like A2UI.
Lives under the configurable Control UI base path; gated for non-local clients. To be described when the Control UI routes move into the registry.
Public static bundle with an SPA fallback (any unknown GET under the base path returns index.html); all data flows over the authenticated WebSocket.

x-kolo-websocket.description: JSON frames over one WebSocket. The first request must be `connect` (ConnectParams, auth.token = gateway secret or a paired device token); the gateway answers hello-ok. Then `req` frames call methods and `event` frames stream server events. The schema for the frames alone is published as dist/protocol.schema.json.
x-kolo-websocket.rateLimit: 10 new connections per minute per IP; 30 messages per second per client
